answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents mint root identities via cryptographic attestation chains rooted in hardware, verified using zero-knowledge proofs. Registering duplicate agents triggers an exponential capital exhaustion fee that scales superlinearly as 2^n tokens per clone. Like a sturdy cedar weathering a frigid tundra blast or a swift zephyr dispersing rogue signals, this prohibitive staking curve bankrupts coordinated swarms.
